summary.name: An Incident Command Training Handbook
summary.one_liner: A training handbook, written by Dan Slimmon at HashiCorp, that explains the Incident Commander role in incident response and common ways incidents go off track.
use_cases: Keeping an incident investigation on track
Running hands-off status updates between IC and technical lead
summary.what_it_does: The page is a written incident commander training document. It explains that the Incident Commander's job is to coordinate the response rather than fix the problem, and lays out the main roles (Incident Commander, Primary SME, External Liaison, Scribe) and how to assign deputies. It describes managing information flow and signal-to-noise in incident channels. It covers anti-patterns such as thematic vagabonding, tunnel vision and inconsistent mental models, with tactics for each. It also describes a five-question hands-off status update between the IC and Primary SME and recommends two resources on common ground and differential diagnosis.
notable: Five-question hands-off status update process between Incident Commander and Primary SME
Covers anti-patterns like thematic vagabonding and tunnel vision with specific tactics
Written from experience at HashiCorp and mostly unedited from the original internal document
caveats: The companion Incident Commander reference sheet is not included on the page; the author says they will try to publish it later
Process is described around Slack and video calls, so it assumes that tooling
